Subject: Deployment follow-up — shared vs dedicated (recap + next steps)

Hi Tom / Sienna —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and recommended next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for your latency/cost/isolation needs.

What we covered (TL;DR):
- Workload: real-time chat support + nightly bulk embeddings for search. Estimated steady-state peak ~120 QPS for short generative requests (<256 tokens); nightly batch ~10M embeddings.
- Primary concerns: noisy neighbor effects on latency, data isolation, and predictable SLAs for peak events.
- Options discussed: Hosted API (fastest to launch), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), Private VPC/on-prem (full control).

Key open questions for you:
1) How strict are your latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for the chat paths?
2) Is cross-tenant data isolation a hard requirement (regulatory/compliance) or is strong logical isolation acceptable?
3) Any firm timelines for go-live where we should target Dedicated capacity cutover?

What I recommend next:
- Short technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Marissa) to go over isolation boundaries and noisy-neighbor mitigations (30–45 mins).
- I attached a short factsheet on SLOs and isolation and our Dedicated pricing sheet to give you concrete numbers.
- If Dedicated looks like the right fit, we can scope a mutual action plan (lead time, capacity size, canary schedule).

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tues 10/20 10:00–10:45am PT or Wed 10/21 2:00–2:45pm PT. Which works?

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Hey Vivek —

Appreciate the summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before we schedule the deep-dive:

1) Noisy neighbor: If we start on Hosted API, what's the practical risk of latency spikes from other tenants? Do you have isolation tiers or priority lanes? We need to avoid tail latency impacting our customer SLAs.

2) SLOs & credits: What are the baseline SLOs for Hosted vs Dedicated? Are SLO credits or SLA remedies part of the Dedicated contract?

3) Dedicated lead time: If we decide Dedicated is required, how long to provision and validate? Can we do a short canary on our production traffic?

4) On-prem/private: We may have a later requirement for Private VPC. Any differences we should plan for from an integration/devops perspective (e.g., KV cache, model artifacts, image versions)?

If you can answer these high-level, we'll pick a time for the deep-dive and prep our infra team.

Thanks,
Tom
Director of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo

Subject: Re: Deployment follow-up — shared vs dedicated (recap + next steps)

Hi Tom — thanks for the great questions. High-level answers below to help you triage before the deep-dive; Marissa / Monica will cover specifics in the call and we can follow with an SRE runbook.

1) Noisy neighbor (Hosted API):
- Hosted is multi-tenant but engineered for predictable tail latency: continuous batching, per-model token prioritization, and per-request routing. For most customers this yields stable p95 latency under normal load.
- For customers with strict tail requirements we recommend Dedicated capacity — a GPU-backed pool reserved to your tenancy which eliminates cross-tenant resource contention. We also offer priority lanes and prefix/KV cache reservation options for Hosted customers on an enterprise plan.

2) SLOs & credits:
- Hosted (standard): best-effort with published performance profiles; operational guarantees for rate limiting and basic availability.
- Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets (example: 99.9% availability and per-route latency objectives; formal SLA and credit schedule in contract).
- We can include explicit SLO language and remedies for Dedicated deals — we'll outline these in the contract addendum.

3) Dedicated lead time & canary:
- Typical lead time: 2–4 weeks from signed order to capacity allocation + validation for mid-sized pools.
- Canary: yes — we run a staged rollout with a canary slice of your traffic (you control the percent) and rollback policies.

4) Private VPC / on-prem planning:
- Private gives you control of the data plane and networking. From an integration perspective you'll see the same API surface; differences are around network egress, KMS integration, and image/version management. Our SEs will provide a migration checklist (KV cache persistence, model artifact pull, metrics/export).

Next steps:
- Lock a 30–45m call with Marissa (SE) to walk SLO examples, capacity sizing, and a canary plan.
- Monica will prepare a short runbook + SRE checklist and share a draft before the call.

Proposed time confirmation? Tue 10/20 10am PT works for us — confirm and I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Vivek
